e28.name: Word, Notion and presentation profile cases

e47.name: The macOS/Linux MCP app and single-process demo support bounded recovery of pending ordinary changes and history when generation, schema, reservation and GC protection are proven. Unknown conditional outcomes, unsupported platforms, storage failures, retention and production recovery remain open. See the recovery plan.

e49.name: The private hosted MCP boundary has static bearer grants, fixed routes, configured upstream credentials, and capacity limits. The document server still needs application authorization and private network placement. OAuth, deployment/TLS, retention, multi-host consistency, and broader failure recovery remain open.

e51.name: Protocol 3 verifies schema identity. Compatible additions can transition without resetting the document; a host can rebuild an open editor. Incompatible migration, application plugin reconstruction and broader failure coverage need separate work.

e53.name: Broader target-editor behavior and real OS IME validation. The reported Lexical/PM merged-grid mismatch is fixed; finite Chrome checks cover merged geometry, hidden data, history and selection.

e55.name: Structural line scans, whole-model comparison/copy, conversion, DOM work, and unexplained tail latency. Stable visible text in moved/required documents now uses at most eight scopes. Whole before/after reads remain for structural changes; eligible large documents compare/verify guarded windows of at most eight top-level nodes. Root child rules, group boundaries and wider spans retain whole verification. Native projection retains unchanged root blocks; changed root containers, Lexical readback, local conversion and whole-model comparisons remain.

e57.name: Two-week scheduled observation and the 30-minute target cadence are not complete.

e59.name: Compiled local packages and isolated consumers pass. Registry publication, API/version policy, migration tools, and release gates remain open.
